JAMA Neurology . https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the CC-BY License. jamaneurol-e212120.pdf Key Points Question Are different patterns of intracranial injury on head computed tomography associated with prognosis after mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI)? Findings In this cohort study, subarachnoid hemorrhage, subdural hematoma, and contusion often co-occurred and were associated with both incomplete recovery and more severe impairment out to 12 months after injury, while intraventricular and/or petechial hemorrhage co-occurred and were associated with more severe impairment up to 12 months after injury; epidural hematoma was associated with incomplete recovery at some points but not with more severe impairment. Some intracranial hemorrhage patterns were more strongly associated with outcomes than previously validated demographic and clinical variables. Meaning In this study, different pathological features on head computed tomography carried different implications for mild traumatic brain injury prognosis to 1 year. extracted_data.document_summary: This longitudinal, observational study aimed to identify and externally validate the association of different pathological computed tomography (CT) features, specifically intracranial injury patterns and hemorrhage subtypes, with adverse outcomes and long-term functional recovery (up to one year post-injury) in mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) patients across two large cohorts, demonstrating that these CT features hold significant and distinct prognostic implications.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study of the prognostic value of pathological computed tomography (CT) features in mild traumatic brain injury
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study analyzing diagnostic head CT findings performed within 24 hours of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) in two large cohorts (TRACK-TBI and CENTER-TBI). CT imaging utilized modern standards (e.g., 64-320 detector rows, <0.3s gantry rotation, <1s whole-head acquisition) to improve diagnostic accuracy, and images were evaluated by board-certified neuroradiologists. No therapeutic intervention or dose-response comparisons were reported, as the focus was on diagnostic and prognostic features.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CT phenotype: Contusion, Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAH), and/or Subdural Hematoma (SDH) cluster

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Strongly associated with incomplete recovery (GOSE scores <8 at 1 year: TRACK-TBI OR=1.80 [95% CI, 1.39-2.33]; CENTER-TBI OR=2.73 [95% CI, 2.18-3.41]) and greater degrees of unfavorable outcomes (GOSE scores <5 at 1 year: TRACK-TBI OR=3.23 [95% CI, 1.59-6.58]; CENTER-TBI OR=1.68 [95% CI, 1.13-2.49]). ORs for GOSE scores <8 ranged from 1.67 (6 months) to 2.22 (2 weeks), and for GOSE <5 from 2.14 (2 weeks) to 3.23 (12 months). Consistent across cohorts.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents acute intracranial lesions and hemorrhage (brain bruising, bleeding between arachnoid/pia mater, or bleeding between dura/arachnoid mater) resulting from head trauma.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) prognosis and recovery assessment, evaluated at 2 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months post-injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts both incomplete recovery and more severe unfavorable outcomes up to 12 months following mTBI.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: CT phenotype: Intraventricular Hemorrhage (IVH) and/or Petechial Hemorrhage cluster

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with more severe impairment/unfavorable outcomes (GOSE scores <5 at 1 year in TRACK-TBI: OR=3.47 [95% CI, 1.66-7.26]; CENTER-TBI: OR=1.82 [95% CI, 1.00-3.29]). ORs for GOSE <5 ranged from 2.37 (3 months) to 3.47 (12 months). Also associated with incomplete recovery in CENTER-TBI at 1 year (OR, 1.71 [95% CI, 1.11-2.62]). Consistent across both cohorts.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents acute intracranial hemorrhage within ventricles or small, scattered hemorrhages, often indicative of rotational acceleration/deceleration injury due to head trauma.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) prognosis and recovery assessment, evaluated at 2 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months post-injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Strong prognostic indicator for more severe impairment, unfavorable outcomes, and incomplete recovery up to 12 months following mTBI, particularly suggesting rotational injury mechanisms.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: associated with incomplete recovery at some points but not with more severe impairment
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Associated with incomplete recovery (GOSE scores <8) at 2 weeks (OR, 3.08 [95% CI, 1.27-7.49]) and 3 months (OR, 2.33 [95% CI, 1.28-4.24]) in TRACK-TBI, and at 1 year in CENTER-TBI (OR, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.02-2.36]). Not associated with greater degrees of unfavorable outcomes (GOSE scores <5) at any point in either study.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents bleeding between the dura mater and the skull, typically arterial in origin, following traumatic brain injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) prognosis and recovery assessment, evaluated at 2 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months post-injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts early incomplete recovery (up to 3 months) post-TBI but is not consistently associated with greater degrees of long-term unfavorable outcomes, suggesting a relatively better prognosis compared to other hemorrhage types.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly associated with incomplete recovery (GOSE scores <8) up to 6 months post-injury: 2 weeks (OR, 2.01 [95% CI, 1.19-3.39]), 3 months (OR, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.00-2.35]), 6 months (OR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.01-2.43]). A trend toward significant association was observed at 12 months (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 0.90-2.03]; P = .14).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents bleeding into the subarachnoid space (the space between the arachnoid membrane and the pia mater covering the brain and spinal cord), typically caused by trauma in this context.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-traumatic brain injury (TBI) recovery assessment, evaluated at 2 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Predicts incomplete recovery up to 6 months post-TBI, with a trend indicating continued association up to 1 year.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Positive head CT result for acute intracranial pathology

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: More likely in men (39.2% vs 32.5% in women; P = .004), individuals with higher education (mean [SD]: positive CT: 13.6 [3.2] years vs negative CT: 13.4 [2.7] years; P = .046), and participants without prior TBI (26.0% vs 34.8% with prior TBI; P < .001). Less likely in Black individuals (23.3% vs 39.7% in White individuals; P < .001).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates the presence of acute structural damage or bleeding within the skull following traumatic brain injury (TBI).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline characteristics and demographics in TRACK-TBI cohort following TBI.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with various demographic and historical factors in TBI patients, potentially indicating differential risk or presentation of injury.
